mainEntity.name: How long do modern dental implants typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern dental implants can function for many years with proper care and maintenance. Reported success rates in clinical studies are generally high over 10-year periods, though individual outcomes vary based on patient health, bone quality, oral hygiene, and other clinical factors. The implant crown may require replacement after 10-15 years due to normal wear. Regular dental maintenance and excellent oral hygiene significantly influence long-term implant success.

mainEntity.name: Are dental implants suitable for everyone who has lost teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whilst dental implants offer excellent outcomes for many patients, individual assessment is essential. Sufficient jawbone density, good oral health, and adequate healing capacity are important factors. Certain medical conditions, medications, or lifestyle factors may affect treatment planning. A comprehensive evaluation helps determine the most appropriate tooth replacement option for each patient's unique circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What made titanium superior to other implant materials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Titanium's unique biocompatible properties allow bone tissue to grow directly onto its surface without inflammatory reaction. Unlike other metals that the body may reject, titanium integrates permanently with jawbone through osseointegration. Its excellent strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and proven long-term stability make it ideal for dental applications requiring permanent integration with living tissue.

mainEntity.name: How has implant surgery evolved since Brånemark's early work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern implant surgery utilises advanced 3D imaging, computer-guided placement, and minimally invasive techniques. These developments have improved accuracy and reduced surgical trauma compared to earlier approaches, and often enable same-day tooth replacement in appropriate cases. Contemporary surface treatments and implant designs promote faster healing and integration compared to early smooth-surface implants. Digital planning allows precise positioning for optimal aesthetic and functional outcomes.

mainEntity.name: Can implants prevent the facial changes associated with tooth loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, dental implants help maintain facial support by preserving jawbone structure. When teeth are lost, the surrounding bone gradually remodels and shrinks, potentially causing facial collapse. Implants provide continued stimulation to jawbone tissue, similar to natural tooth roots. This helps maintain bone volume and facial dimensions, supporting a more youthful appearance compared to removable dentures alone.

mainEntity.name: What role did early dental pioneers play in implant development?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early pioneers like Dr Leonard Linkow, Dr Stefano Tramonte, and others contributed significantly to implant design and surgical techniques during the 1960s-1980s. Their clinical experience and innovations in implant shapes, surfaces, and placement methods helped refine the procedures we use today. Their collaborative research and case documentation established many principles still followed in contemporary implant dentistry.
